title: the registry promotion wiring
audit_comment: THE REGISTRY PROMOTION WIRING - the tooling round of the creature-registry promotion (the user-set seam, 2026-10-23). The engine gains spec-declared new-file emission (data_files - idempotent by existence, counted in the applied/already census), so R792 can write all 65 .lua defs in one pass - the MM1 precedent (monsters2lua.py generated all 408 defs from the merged @-record file). The counts ride as pins: OA 39, WSG 18, MOP Appendix III 8, total 65, the registry growing 408 -> 473 live in the battery. The two zero-record adjustments ride as schema fields: the DMO legendary ladder as a rank field, the MOP Appendix II analogue system as a transform field. The pin headers stay the print-fidelity record.

banner.title: THE REGISTRY PROMOTION WIRING - the engine data-files extension and the promotion doctrine pins: the tooling for the all-in-one R792
banner.provenance: The tooling round of the promotion seam. Verified repo state at 3ff2f2a: the live registry holds 408 MM1 defs loaded by the Lua 5.4 C API loader; the five pin-only creature sets (OA Chapter 12, WSG animals, DMO ladder, MOP Appendices II and III) have zero runtime wiring. This round lands the engine extension (data_files) and the doctrine pins; R792 writes the 65 defs in one pass, lands the schema adjustments (the WSG load fields, the DMO rank field, the MOP analogue transform field), and the battery census grows live: loaded 408 -> 473. The WSG mount and fish headers get one look before the R792 cut.

file_patches.note: the engine data-files extension (spec-declared new-file emission, the R774/R775 tooling precedent)
file_patches.to:
# ---------- the data files (the R791 tooling
# extension): spec-declared NEW files written
# verbatim - a path plus a content, idempotent
# by existence, each one counted in the
# applied/already census so the double-run
# gate covers them exactly like a file patch
# (the registry promotion class: 65 .lua defs
# ride R792)
for df in S.get('data_files', []):
    p = df['path']
    if os.path.exists(p):
        already.append('data: %s' % p)
    else:
        writes.append((p, df['content']))
        applied.append('data: %s' % p)

# ---------- the idempotency gate (the R420 lesson) ----------
